71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)

80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i
135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
141	      (ht' i)
142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem

146	consumes. -/
147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,

153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/

162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice

281	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
282	  (HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose
283	
284	/-- **THE PROJECT'S CENTRAL OPEN OBLIGATION — expected to stay open.**
285	
286	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main` + Cor `cor:algsch`: for a smooth proper geometrically
287	integral curve `C` over an *arbitrary* field `k`, the **étale-sheafified**
288	relative Picard functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` (`PicScheme.picEt`,
289	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean`) is representable by a `k`-scheme that is separated
290	and locally of finite type — a disjoint union of open quasi-projective
291	`k`-subschemes. All three conjuncts are parts of that one theorem, which is
292	why they are bundled.
293	
294	**There is no hypothesis on `C(k)`, and that is the point.** This statement is
295	the one the challenge asks for: `AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` binds
296	`Jacobian C` for a curve with no rational point, so a representability input
297	carrying `[HasRationalPoint C]` answers a different question. The conditional
298	form survives beside this one as `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` below, clearly
299	labelled as strictly weaker.
300	
301	**Why sheafifying is what makes an unconditional statement possible.** The
302	unsheafified functor `picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is *not*
303	representable over a general field — it is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2
304	L1292–L1302), and a representable functor is a sheaf for any subcanonical
305	topology. So an unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` would be a
306	FALSE statement, not merely an unproved one. Against `picEt` it is Kleiman's own
307	theorem. `PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` records the sheaf property that makes
308	the difference, and it is proved rather than assumed.
309	
310	**Expected to stay open, and that is the honest state rather than a defect.**
311	Discharging it means formalising the Kleiman §4 existence proof: the Abel-map
312	slice `Div^d_{C/k} → Pic^d_{C/k}` is a smooth proper equivalence relation whose
313	quotient is a scheme (`smoothProperQuotient`, itself gated on
314	`HasSmoothProperQuotient` because Mathlib `v4.31` has no quasi-projectivity
315	vocabulary), together with `Div` representability (Kleiman §3 Thm `th:repDiv`,
316	which needs the Quot scheme). Neither input is available; the project reaches
317	this statement rather than proving it, and it is the single named `sorry` that
318	the whole Jacobian headline rests on. Do not replace it with a weaker
319	conditional statement to make a count go down.
320	
321	This is the **sole** `sorry` of the seam: everything else below — the
322	representing scheme `PicSchemeEt`, its representability, local finiteness,
323	separatedness and group-scheme structure, the comparison class
324	`PicEtComparisonIso` and the conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — is
325	derived from it.
326	
327	**Why the second conjunct is bundled here rather than given its own `sorry`.**
328	Clause (1) is Kleiman §4; clause (2) is Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 (`th:comp`): given a
329	section, the comparison `picSharp C → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is an isomorphism. Both are
330	theorems of the same paper and neither is formalised. They are stated as one
331	named obligation on purpose: the `picSharp`-shaped consumer interface
332	(`HasPicScheme`, and through it the tangent-space chain and the `k̄` Albanese
333	witness) needs clause (2) to exist at all, and splitting it out would report the
334	Jacobian headline as resting on *six* open obligations where the mathematics has
335	five. The bundling adds no strength — clause (2) is conditional on a section, so
336	it says nothing about a pointless curve — and it keeps the frontier count honest
337	in both directions. `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` measures the result rather
338	than asserting it. -/
339	theorem fgaPicardRepresentability {k : Type u} [Field k]
340	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
341	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
342	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
343	    (∃ (X : Over (Spec (.of k))),
344	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
345	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom)
346	      ∧ (HasRationalPoint C → IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)) :=
347	  sorry
348	
349	/-- **The étale representability gate**, as a `Prop`-class so that consumers can
350	quantify over it as a hypothesis and stay kernel-clean.
351	
352	Unlike the legacy `HasPicScheme`, this class carries **no** hypothesis on
353	`C(k)`: its unique producer `instHasPicSchemeEt` is unconditional. It is the
354	carrier of the project's central open obligation. -/
355	class HasPicSchemeEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
356	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
357	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : Prop where
358	  has_pic_scheme_et : ∃ (X : Over (Spec (.of k))),
359	    Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
360	      LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom
361	
362	/-- The étale gate fires for **every** smooth proper geometrically integral
363	curve, with no rational-point hypothesis — which is the whole content of the
364	owner decision of 2026-07-28. Its mathematics is
365	`fgaPicardRepresentability`, the one open obligation. -/
366	instance instHasPicSchemeEt {k : Type u} [Field k]
367	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
368	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
369	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : HasPicSchemeEt C :=
370	  ⟨(fgaPicardRepresentability C).1⟩
371	
372	/-- **The Picard scheme `Pic_{C/k}` over an arbitrary base field**: the scheme
373	representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor.
374	
375	This is the honest `Pic_{C/k}` of the project — available for every smooth
376	proper geometrically integral curve, with no hypothesis on `C(k)`. The legacy
377	`PicScheme` (representing the unsheafified `picSharp`) exists only under a
378	rational point and is retained for the consumers written against it. -/
379	noncomputable def PicSchemeEt {k : Type u} [Field k]
380	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
381	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
382	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
383	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
384	  (HasPicSchemeEt.has_pic_scheme_et (C := C)).choose
385	
386	/-- **Representability of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` by `Pic_{C/k}`, over an arbitrary
387	field**: the natural bijection `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)`.
388	
389	The étale-formulation replacement for `PicScheme.representable`. Consumers of
390	the tangent-space chain should compose with *this* `homEquiv`; the `picSharp`
391	version is available only under `[HasRationalPoint C]`. -/

393	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
394	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
395	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
396	    (PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy (PicSchemeEt C) :=
397	  Classical.choice (HasPicSchemeEt.has_pic_scheme_et (C := C)).choose_spec.1

151	    Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
152	  (CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).obj
153	    (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
154	
155	/-- **The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, as a standalone statement.**
156	
157	The underlying presheaf of `PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` satisfies the sheaf axiom
158	for the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled
159	object, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a
160	representing scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being
161	represented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any
162	subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
163	exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).
164	
165	Proved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/
166	theorem etaleSheaf_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
167	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
168	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
169	  (etaleSheaf C).property

171	/-- **The comparison map** `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, i.e. the unit of the
172	sheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.
173	
174	Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a
175	`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an
176	arbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,
177	which is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/
178	noncomputable def toEtaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
179	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
180	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
181	  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
182	
183	/-- The universal property of the sheafification, in the form consumers use:
184	every morphism from the relative Picard presheaf to (the underlying presheaf
185	of) an étale sheaf factors uniquely through `toEtaleSheaf`.
186	
187	This is what makes `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` the *canonical* choice rather than one
188	sheaf among many, and it is the step that turns a representing scheme for the
189	sheaf into a universal receiver of relative Picard classes. -/
190	noncomputable def etaleSheafHomEquiv {k : Type u} [Field k]
191	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
192	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
193	    (G : Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
194	    (etaleSheaf C ⟶ G) ≃ (PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ G.obj) :=
195	  ((CategoryTheory.sheafificationAdjunction (etaleTopologyOver k)
196	    AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).homEquiv (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) G)
197	
198	end PicSharp

202	/-! ## §3. The set-valued functor that gets represented -/
203	
204	/-- **The functor whose representability is the project's central obligation**:
205	the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor with its group structure
206	forgotten,
207	
208	```
209	picEt C : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1),   T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T).
210	```
211	
212	Representability is a statement about the underlying set-valued functor; the
213	group structure is transported back onto the representing scheme by Yoneda
214	(`PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`), exactly as for the unsheafified
215	`picSharp`.
216	
217	Contrast with `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget`: that functor is
218	representable only under a rational-point hypothesis (it is not even a
219	Zariski sheaf otherwise), whereas *this* one is the object of Kleiman §4
220	Thm. `th:main` and its representability needs no hypothesis on `C(k)`. -/
221	noncomputable def picEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
222	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
223	    (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
224	  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}
225	
226	/-- The comparison `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` of set-valued functors, the
227	set-level shadow of `PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf`. An isomorphism under a
228	`k`-rational point (Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5), a comparison in general.
229	
230	The source is written out as `PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _` rather than as
231	`picSharp C`, which is the *same functor by definition* but is declared in the
232	downstream `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (that file imports this one, so
233	the name is not available here). -/
234	noncomputable def picEtComparison {k : Type u} [Field k]
235	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
236	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
237	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} ⟶ picEt C :=
238	  CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskerRight (PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C)
239	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})
240	
241	/-- **`picEt` is an étale sheaf of sets.**
242	
243	The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` survives forgetting the group structure,
244	because the forgetful functor `AddCommGrpCat ⥤ Type` preserves the limits the
245	sheaf condition is stated by. Together with the fact that a representable
246	functor is a sheaf for a subcanonical topology, this is the structural reason
247	the representability obligation is *consistent* as stated — which the
248	unsheafified `picSharp` version was not, absent a rational point. -/
249	theorem picEt_isSheaf_forget {k : Type u} [Field k]
250	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
251	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
252	    Presieve.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (picEt C) := by
253	  have h := ((CategoryTheory.sheafCompose (etaleTopologyOver k)
254	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})).obj (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C)).property
255	  rw [CategoryTheory.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type] at h
256	  exact h

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeZero
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap
8	
9	/-!
10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
11	
12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
33	-/
34	
35	set_option autoImplicit false
36	
37	universe u
38	
39	open CategoryTheory
40	
41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
42	
43	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
44	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
45	
46	noncomputable section
47	
48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
49	
50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
57	
58	section DegAt
59	
60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
61	
62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
63	@[simp]
64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
67	
68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
75	
76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
81	  rfl
82	
83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
92	
93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'
98	
99	end DegAt
100	
101	/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/
102	
103	variable (C) in
104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
109	    degAt lam t = 0}
110	  one_mem' := by
111	    intro K _ _ t
112	    exact degAt_one t
113	  mul_mem' := by
114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
116	  inv_mem' := by
117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
